title: [bug] gonk-gate envArg uppercased param names -> every dispatch arg empty, no formula ever poured
description: cmd/gonk-gate/main.go's envArg read GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_<UPPERCASE(name)>, but Gas City sets GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_<name> with the [order.params] key verbatim (internal/webhookmatch/extract.go ExecEnvVars is a plain map copy over declared param names). Every gonk param is lower_snake_case, so every arg read back empty and gonk-dispatch failed with 'unknown trigger; pouring nothing' trigger="" -- after meter had already been asked, so it burned a budget decision and poured nothing.
design: Read the verbatim name first; keep the uppercase spelling as a fallback so a future Gas City that normalizes keys still works.

title: gonk-meter LiteLLM adapter broken against real v1.92.0: spend poller (v2 date format + response envelope + pagination) and admin update-by-alias (/key/info)
description:
Found by Plan 06 L2 (test/component: first contact between internal/meter/litellm and a REAL LiteLLM ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:v1.92.0). Two independent, reproducible, FATAL defects. The adapters were written against docs + httptest mocks (which returned the WRONG shape), so both slipped through Plan 03.

=== BUG A (spend poller, FATAL) -- internal/meter/litellm/spendsource_http.go ===
Meter can NEVER ingest spend against real v1.92.0 => never synced => Ready() never true => every budgeted /decide defers forever.
1. fetchPage sends start_date/end_date as time.RFC3339 ("2026-07-01T00:00:00Z"). Real /spend/logs/v2 rejects it: HTTP 400 {"message":"Invalid date format: 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z. Expected: 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'"}. FIX: format as "2006-01-02" (or "2006-01-02 15:04:05").
2. Since() does json.Unmarshal(body,&entries) with entries []logEntry, but v2 returns an OBJECT {"data":[...],"total","page","page_size","total_pages"}, NOT a bare array. Even with dates fixed, unmarshal fails. FIX: decode {"data":[]logEntry, total, page, total_pages}.
3. Pagination reads header.Get("X-Next-Page") (absent in v2). Real pagination is body fields page/total_pages. Only page 1 is ever read -> silent drop past page_size. FIX: loop while page < total_pages.
Root cause the tests missed it: internal/meter/litellm/spendsource_test.go mock returns a bare `[ {...} ]` array and ignores the query dates entirely.

=== BUG B (admin update-by-alias, breaks re-provisioning) -- internal/meter/litellm/admin_http.go ===
EnsureKey is idempotent-by-alias: /key/generate on an existing alias returns 400 "Key with alias 'X' already exists" (alreadyExists() matches), then updateByAlias() runs:
1. GET /key/info?key_alias=<alias> returns 404 {"message":"Key not found in database"}. v1.92.0 /key/info accepts ONLY ?key=<token>, NOT ?key_alias=. => EnsureKey errors on the SECOND ensure for any project (every budget change / ReconcileKeys tick / re-register).
2. /key/info shape is nested: {"key":..., "info":{"key_alias":...,"max_budget":...}} -- decodeKeyResponse reads TOP-LEVEL key_alias (would be empty). 
FIX: look the token up another way (LiteLLM has /key/list?key_alias=; or GET /key/info?key=<token> once the token is known; or store the token). Parse the nested .info shape.

=== VERIFIED GOOD (no change needed) ===
- HARD DOOR CLOSES: $1.00 key on glm ($2/1M), 100k tok/call = $0.20; call 6 refused HTTP 429 budget_exceeded "Current cost: 1.0, Max budget: 1.0". Zero overshoot.
- budget_duration "1mo" IS a UTC CALENDAR month: key created 2026-07-19, budget_reset_at 2026-08-01T00:00:00+00:00. (P3-2 OK, not rolling-30-days.)
- /model/info returns input_cost_per_token matching configured prices (qwen 2.5e-07, glm 2e-06, sonnet 6e-06) -> synthetic prices agree, catalog drift checkable (P3-4/P3-8).
- Dedicated proxy-admin key SUFFICES (P3-6): a plain generated key gets 401 on /key/generate & /spend/logs/v2, but a key issued to a /user/new user_role=proxy_admin does all admin calls -> master key NOT required.
- metadata NOT forwarded upstream (stub saw only [messages,model]) -> stub log is a VOLUME check only, attribution must come from v2 spend_logs_metadata.
- /key/delete {"key_aliases":[...]} works, returns {"deleted_keys":[...]}, token refused (401) IMMEDIATELY after.
- Also observed: detailed LiteLLM_SpendLogs table write lag is large/unreliable in single-node podman (rows often not visible within 100s even at proxy_batch_write_at:1; after a proxy restart, completions produced no rows in-window) while the key-level budget counter is immediate. P3-3 (spend-log lag vs max_spend_staleness) must be measured through the real code path AFTER Bug A is fixed.

Evidence + full reproduction in docs/spikes/litellm-verified.md. Blocks Plan 06 Task 5 (L2 suite cannot go green until the adapter speaks v2).
close_reason: Fixed + live-verified against real LiteLLM v1.92.0 + adversarially reviewed (no credential blanking), merged to main (bef6684). Spend poller reads /spend/logs/v2 (YYYY-MM-DD dates, {data,...} envelope, page/total_pages); updateByAlias resolves via /key/list then /key/update; service.go preserves the stored KeyRef on empty token. Mocks rewritten to the real v2 contract. Follow-ups: gonk-4nk, gonk-0qi.

title: Every onboarded project bricks: ReserveIfFits applies cost gate to zero-cost local rungs
description: P0 money-path defect found by Plan 06 L1 (test/integration wiring real intake+meter). The onboarding default ships monthly_cost_usd:0 + ladder:[qwen-local] (local, zero-cost rung; spec 5.3). pkg/rung/decide.go:246 correctly SKIPS the cost gate for zero-cost rungs (if spec.EstCostUSD>0 && !rem.FitsCost). But internal/meter/store/memory.go:146 AND postgres.go:428 apply the cost check UNCONDITIONALLY (if !rem.FitsCost(r.CostUSD)||...), and pkg/budget/remaining.go:119 FitsCost returns false whenever MonthlyCostUSD<=0 regardless of est. So ReserveIfFits asks FitsCost(0) against a $0 ceiling -> false -> rejects a reservation that holds ZERO real dollars, even though Decide just said 'run'. Result: POST /v1/policy/decide returns defer/monthly-cost-exhausted for every freshly-onboarded project -- dead on arrival. Affects BOTH store backends (postgres is the real ledger). Latent because no meter test registered a $0-cost budget with a local ladder. FIX: mirror Decide's gate in both ReserveIfFits impls -> if (r.CostUSD>0 && !rem.FitsCost(r.CostUSD)) || !rem.FitsMonthTokens(r.Tokens) || !rem.FitsTaskTokens(r.Tokens). A zero-cost reservation holds no real dollars so it must always clear the cost leg (token gates still enforce the token budget via synthetic pricing). Add a storetest guard: 'zero-cost local rung reserves under a $0 cost budget'. Money-path -> adversarial review before merge.
close_reason: Fixed + adversarially reviewed + merged to main (8bf5381). Both stores skip the cost leg for zero-cost rungs; verified on real Postgres (fail-before/pass-after, priced rungs still rejected, overspend race 0/10, idempotency intact). Optional future hardening: validateFiniteMoney could also reject CostUSD<0 (unreachable in prod).

title: [bug] Controller never set GONK_BEAD_REPO_DIR -> in-memory bead store, parked beads never unpark
description: The chart set no GONK_BEAD_REPO_DIR on the controller, so gonk-gate's store() fell back to beadstore.NewMemory(). gonk-gate's own warning calls this 'fine for a smoke test, never for the controller': the store does not survive a single invocation, so a parked bead is never unparked by gonk-sweep and an outcome is never reported -- silently, with no error. Fixed by setting GONK_BEAD_REPO_DIR=/city (bd is on PATH in the controller image and the city's bd store lives there; verified live in-pod).

title: [bug] gcapi.ParsePrivateKey TrimSpace corrupts ~4.6% of raw ed25519 keys
description: ParsePrivateKey ran bytes.TrimSpace over RAW ed25519 key material. Key bytes are uniform random, so the first or last byte is an ASCII whitespace value (6 of 256) about 4.6% of the time; those bytes were trimmed and the key then failed length validation with 'raw length 63 is neither a 32-byte seed nor a 64-byte key'. In the field this is an unreproducible ~1-in-22 controller/intake startup failure whose error message points nowhere near the cause. Found because TestParsePrivateKeyRaw64 generates a fresh key per run and so trips it roughly 1 run in 22.
design: Take exact-length (32 or 64 byte) input VERBATIM; keep bytes.TrimSpace only as the fallback for text files written with a trailing newline. Two new deterministic tests cover every whitespace byte at both ends in both key lengths, plus one proving the trailing-newline text case still parses.
acceptance_criteria: go test ./pkg/gcapi/ -count=20 passes; raw keys with leading/trailing whitespace bytes round-trip byte for byte.
close_reason: Fixed in 383ada0 on feat/gonk-712-minimal-opencode-leg: exact-length input taken verbatim, TrimSpace kept only as the text-file fallback; TestParsePrivateKeyKeepsWhitespaceBytes + TestParsePrivateKeyStillTrimsTextFiles added.

title: Chart never wires gonk-agent image into gc k8s session provider (GC_K8S_IMAGE unset) -> triage session cannot spawn agent pod
description: gascity k8s session provider (internal/runtime/k8s/provider.go @ GASCITY_REF) reads GC_K8S_IMAGE (required for Start), GC_K8S_NAMESPACE, GC_K8S_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, GC_K8S_PREBAKED. gonk.controllerEnv sets none. componentImages.agent.tag exists in values.yaml but is DEAD CONFIG - consumed nowhere. Result: dispatched triage order reaches controller but the session provider has no image to spawn, so no real agent pod / no triage comment ever. Discovered while proving gonk-712 e2e. Fix: wire componentImages.agent -> GC_K8S_IMAGE + GC_K8S_NAMESPACE=Release.Namespace + GC_K8S_SERVICE_ACCOUNT=gc-agent + GC_K8S_PREBAKED=true into the controller container env; ensure gc-agent SA carries the registry pull secret.
design:
Full gap list blocking gonk v1 e2e triage-comment, from reading gascity k8s session provider (internal/runtime/k8s/{provider,pod}.go @ GASCITY_REF) + gonk chart/pack/image:
1. GC_K8S_IMAGE/GC_K8S_NAMESPACE/GC_K8S_SERVICE_ACCOUNT/GC_K8S_PREBAKED unset in gonk.controllerEnv; componentImages.agent.tag is dead config (consumed nowhere).
2. No agent command defined: provider runs cfg.Command inside 'tmux new-session'; pack sets no command (agent_defaults only sets wake_mode), so gonk's opencode/entrypoint is never invoked.
3. Agent image has NO tmux (Dockerfile installs git/ca-certificates/jq only) -> tmux new-session fails.
4. Provider OVERRIDES image ENTRYPOINT (Command=[sh -c], Args=[tmuxCmd]) -> gonk-agent-entrypoint.sh (renders litellm overlay, execs opencode) never runs; and GONK_LITELLM_URL/GONK_LITELLM_KEY_FILE/GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_MODEL/GC_WEBHOOK_ARG_METADATA_JSON (entrypoint hard-requires all) are unplumbed to the session pod.
5. gc-agent SA needs registry pull secret (pod.go sets no imagePullSecrets).
CONCLUSION: current opencode+gascity-k8s integration is incomplete; e2e triage-comment cannot succeed without finishing it. Likely the motivation behind the deferred broker-lite/proposed-effects redesign (origin/design-gonk-agent-harness). Prior L3/smoke never reached session spawn.
notes: LIVE RUN found a stack of never-run-path bugs, each hiding the next (all fixed on branch feat/gonk-712-minimal-opencode-leg): (1) intake OrderRequest missing bead_id -> dispatch 422; (2) controller missing GONK_METER_URL/GONK_METER_TOKEN_FILE + meter-api mount -> gonk-gate exit 2; (3) formula orders gonk-triage/scaffold/mention had no [order.params] -> supervisor rejects webhook orders; (4) Gas City strips inherited env keys containing TOKEN/SECRET/etc (internal/execenv.IsSensitiveKey) from exec orders, so GONK_METER_TOKEN_FILE never reached the dispatch exec -> fixed with explicit [order.env] (path, not secret). KNOWN REMAINING (v2-broker territory): same stripping drops GONK_LITELLM_KEY/GONK_BOT_TOKEN so session creds arrive empty -- a secret VALUE cannot be a static [order.env], and gascity mounts no gonk secrets into session pods (only git-credentials->GITHUB_TOKEN, one slot, two creds needed). Deploy-time: webhook secret must be >=32 bytes; .agent/ added to project 75 main to reach valid (scaffold agent is itself an opencode session). BLOCKED on the actual model call by Bailey GPU wedge (inference hangs; hardware/gitops).

title: Chart pins nonexistent Dolt image tag v1.43.0 -> ImagePullBackOff on any real install
description: Found by Plan 06 L3 (first real helm install of chart/gonk on the orac cluster). Every chart/gonk/ci/*.yaml and internal/charttest/charttest.go Minimum() pin dolt.image.tag=v1.43.0, but docker.io/dolthub/dolt-sql-server has NO v1.43.0 tag (DoltHub tags carry no 'v' prefix). The Dolt pod ImagePullBackOffs; the whole chart can't install. Invisible to render/kubeconform goldens (they don't pull). The working tag is 2.1.7 (matches the controller image's DOLT_VERSION / dolt CLI, so beads data format is consistent). FIX: bump dolt.image.tag v1.43.0 -> 2.1.7 in all ci/*.yaml + charttest Minimum(); regen goldens. Verified 2.1.7 pulls + runs in the L3 deploy (kubectl set image ...:2.1.7 -> Dolt+controller Ready).

title: Meter key-provisioning: unserialized resolveProject can split-brain the virtual key under overlapping tickers
description: Found by gonk-huy review. resolveProject/resolveKeyRef/ReconcileKeys/Reresolve take no per-project lock (keyedMutex is used only in Decide). Two ticker goroutines (ReconcileKeys main.go:134 + Reresolve main.go:147) can both enter the RotateKey (delete+generate) branch for a StateKeyMissing project before either commits Active: T2's delete destroys the key T1 just minted, the sink ends up holding T1's dead token while LiteLLM's live key is T2's -> agent 401s with NO self-heal (later reresolves take the preserve path, keeping the stale sink token). Narrow window (key-missing + overlapping tickers + both pre-commit), and the missing serialization predates the gonk-huy fix, but the new working delete+generate rotate branch is what makes it destructive. FIX: serialize resolveProject per project (reuse s.locks keyedMutex), or make rotate idempotency-safe. service.go:311-341,445,1227.

title: pack gonk-dispatch trigger=manual but /run endpoint fires only trigger=webhook (422)
description: pack/orders/gonk-dispatch.toml declares trigger='manual', but the supervisor /v0/city/<city>/order/<name>/run endpoint at GASCITY_REF fires ONLY trigger='webhook' orders -> gonk-intake's dispatch POST returns 422 'webhook-rejected'. As written, gonk-intake -> gonk-dispatch cannot fire via /run. FIX: reconcile the trigger taxonomy -- likely set gonk-dispatch (and gonk-sweep?) trigger='webhook', but confirm against gascity's formulas-v2 trigger model that 'webhook' is the correct type for an HTTP-fired order and that it doesn't break other pack semantics. Plan 04 (pack) scope. Found by Task 0.5 re-smoke; evidence in chart/gonk/smoke/gc-controller-smoke.md.
close_reason: Fixed + proven end-to-end in-cluster (merge c2b474a): bootable controller image, ed25519 authenticated dispatch, webhook triggers, chart wiring + 5 boot blockers. Clean from-scratch boot confirmed.

title: pkg/gcapi omits required X-GC-Request CSRF header; every dispatch POST gets 403
description: gc's order-run mutation endpoint requires the X-GC-Request header (csrf: 'X-GC-Request header required'). pkg/gcapi/client.go:126-127 sends only Content-Type + User-Agent, so every gonk-intake -> gonk-dispatch POST /v0/city/<city>/order/<name>/run returns 403 as written. FIX: add the X-GC-Request header (presence sufficed in smoke: adding it advanced 403->422). Verify the exact expected value/semantics vs gascity at GASCITY_REF. Plan 02 (pkg/gcapi) scope. Found by Task 0.5 re-smoke; evidence in chart/gonk/smoke/gc-controller-smoke.md.

title: Chart controller wiring points at dead port 9443; needs supervisor.toml + repoint to [supervisor].port
description:
Task 0.5 re-smoke (fixed image) proved the order-run route /v0/city//order//run lives on the MACHINE-WIDE supervisor unified API, NOT the per-city [api] 9443. Under 'gc supervisor run' the city [api] 9443 is IGNORED (logged verbatim) and the supervisor binds 8372 LOOPBACK only -> the chart's Service/probes/gonk.supervisorURL point at a port nothing binds; cross-pod dispatch is unreachable. FIX (Plan 05 Task 6.5 follow-up): mount a ~/.gc/supervisor.toml with [supervisor] bind=0.0.0.0, port=

, allow_mutations=true, allowed_hosts=[], and write-auth; repoint controller Service + httpGet probes + gonk.supervisorURL at [supervisor].port; keep command 'gc supervisor run'. Measured gates: non-loopback is read-only unless allow_mutations; allowed_hosts must list exact Host (port stripped, no wildcard) else 421; allow_mutations+non-loopback+no-key is fail-closed unless write_auth_allow_unverified acks it. Evidence in chart/gonk/smoke/gc-controller-smoke.md (dispatch endpoint section).
close_reason: Fixed + proven end-to-end in-cluster (merge c2b474a): bootable controller image, ed25519 authenticated dispatch, webhook triggers, chart wiring + 5 boot blockers. Clean from-scratch boot confirmed.

NOT pushed yet. In-cluster confirm is BLOCKED on the 3 dispatch-wiring bugs found during the re-smoke (chart port repoint + gcapi CSRF header + pack trigger). Do NOT close until pushed + in-cluster order-run works end-to-end.

title: Report LiteLLM unbounded /spend/logs OOM DoS to upstream
description:
Found while verifying gonk's attribution chain against the live LiteLLM (v1.92.0): an unbounded GET /spend/logs (no start_date) OOM-killed the proxy (2Gi, exit 137, ~90s outage). Full write-up ready to file at docs/upstream/litellm-spend-logs-unbounded-dos.md.

Owner will file it. Decision needed before filing: public GitHub issue vs security@berri.ai. That hinges on ONE unverified question -- whether a low-privilege tenant virtual key (get_spend_routes, no internal-user role) can reach the unscoped full-table path, or only master/admin can. If a tenant key can, it's a privilege-limited DoS -> security@. If only admin, it's an ops hardening bug -> public issue. The probe to settle this was not completed (transient cluster TLS timeout; owner redirected).

Not fixed upstream: identical on v1.92.0 (latest stable) and main; a bounded /spend/logs/v2 exists but the legacy endpoint was only marked [DEPRECATED] in a docstring, not bounded. Prior art: issue #14218 (closed not-planned as a feature request, not framed as DoS).

Relevance to gonk: gonk-meter polls /spend/logs, so this is also a hard requirement on our side -- always query with a bounded window, never a naked query. Recorded in docs/environment.md and to be enforced in plan 03.

title: Meter key preserve-branch does not self-heal a deleted k8s Secret (dangling KeyRef)
description: Found by gonk-huy review (nit). resolveKeyRef's empty-token preserve branch trusts prev.KeyRef.SecretName != '' without confirming the k8s Secret still exists. If an operator deletes the Secret out-of-band while the LiteLLM key survives, every subsequent re-register takes update->preserve and never re-mints -> project stays broken with no self-heal. Narrow (requires out-of-band deletion). FIX: on the preserve branch, verify the Secret exists (keysink get) and re-mint if absent. service.go:326-341.

title: Research GitLab Duo 'flows' as a growth direction for gonk's pack sequences
description:
POST-MVP research (do NOT start until gonk MVP is delivered and running). GitLab Duo Agent Platform has configurable 'flows' (foundational_flows) that are ordered step-sequences for performing a kind of work -- conceptually very similar to what gonk expresses as pack formulas + orders (the order of steps to perform a unit of work). Potential growth direction: align with / interoperate with / learn from Duo flows rather than only our bespoke Gas City pack sequences.

Trailhead: https://docs.gitlab.com/user/duo_agent_platform/flows/foundational_flows/

Owner flagged 2026-07-17 during Plan 04 execution. Follow-up: read the Duo flows docs, compare the flow model to gonk's formula/order DAG (pkg/gate outcome gates, the two-gate budget model, the deterministic no-LLM-judge ladder), and assess whether gonk should adopt, bridge to, or differentiate from Duo flows.
